title: SANWO-OLU SEEKS AFRICAN CAPITAL AND PRIVATE SECTOR PARTICIPATION TO SAVE CONTINENT’S FORESTS.
author: moel
excerpt: Lagos State Governor, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu on Tuesday called for increased mobilisation of African capital and private-sector investment to protect the continent’s rapidly declin...
content:
Lagos State Governor, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu on Tuesday called for increased mobilisation of African capital and private-sector investment to protect the continent’s rapidly declining forest resources, stressing that sustainable forestry must become a major driver of economic growth, job creation, livelihoods and climate resilience.
Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu made the call through the Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr Tokunbo Wahab at the High-Level Lunch Debate/Business Roundtable on the Future of African Forestry, held at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja, Lagos.
[caption id="attachment_7426" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Executive Secretary-CEO. Africa Forest Forum, Prof. Labode Popoola; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Former Vice President and Chairman Sustainable Forest Management for Africa, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo; Chairman Governing Council, Africa Forest Forum, Prof. Larwanou Mahamane and the Controller of Environment, Federal Ministry of Environment, Mrs. Olabimpe Adenaike, during the high-level launch debate/business roundtable on the future of African forestry, held on the 8th of September, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel, GRA Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
Sanwo-Olu, while welcoming participants to Lagos for the high-level dialogue, said Africa could no longer afford to treat its forests solely as environmental resources, but must recognise their enormous economic potential and develop innovative financing mechanisms to protect and sustainably manage them.
He noted that Africa is losing nearly four million hectares of forest annually, while funding for sustainable forest management is becoming increasingly difficult to secure.
He described the situation as a major challenge but also an opportunity for African countries to develop new approaches to financing conservation and responsible utilisation of forest resources.
“We must begin to see our forests not only as environmental assets, but as economic assets—capable of supporting sustainable businesses, green investment, livelihoods, food security and climate resilience.” he said.
The Governor  welcomed the proposal for the establishment of an African Forestry Trust Fund, describing it as an important step towards giving the continent greater ownership of the financing of forest protection and sustainable management.
[caption id="attachment_7425" align="alignleft" width="2019"] L-R: Executive Secretary-CEO. Africa Forest Forum, Prof. Labode Popoola; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Former Vice President and Chairman Sustainable Forest Management for Africa, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo and Chairman Governing Council, Africa Forest Forum, Prof. Larwanou Mahamane, during the high-level launch debate/business roundtable on the future of African forestry, held on the 8th of September, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel, GRA Ikeja, Lagos State[/caption]
According to him, while Africa must continue to welcome international partnerships, the continent must equally build strong institutions capable of mobilising domestic and African capital and attracting global investments towards its own development priorities.
Sanwo-Olu emphasised the need for stronger private-sector participation in forestry, noting that government alone could not provide the resources required to address the scale of the continent’s forestry challenges.
He called for greater collaboration among governments, investors, financial institutions, entrepreneurs, development partners and local communities to develop viable forestry projects that would deliver both environmental and economic returns.
The Governor stressed that properly managed forests could become significant sources of employment and investment while strengthening food security, protecting communities from the impacts of climate change and ensuring a healthier environment for future generations.
He urged stakeholders at the roundtable to move beyond reaffirming their commitment to sustainable forestry and focus on concrete measures for mobilising capital, building effective partnerships and implementing projects that would secure the future of Africa’s forests.
Sanwo-Olu also reaffirmed Lagos State’s readiness to support initiatives that promote sustainable development and responsible investment across the continent, stressing that the ultimate objective of sustainable forest management must be to improve the quality of life of African people.
He expressed optimism that the deliberations would produce tangible outcomes and practical strategies capable of transforming Africa’s forestry sector into a sustainable platform for environmental protection, economic opportunity and continental resilience.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina,
Director,
Public Affairs,
 MOE&WR

title: LAGOS CHARGES  COASTAL COMMUNITIES ON RESPONSIBLE ENVIRONMENTAL PRACTICES TO CURB FLOODING
author: moel
excerpt: The Lagos State Government has called on residents of coastal communities to embrace responsible environmental practices, improve waste management habits and take collective actio...
content:
The Lagos State Government has called on residents of coastal communities to embrace responsible environmental practices, improve waste management habits and take collective action to reduce flooding and protect the environment.
This call was made by the  Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen on Wednesday while speaking at the Environmental Education Advocacy Programme held at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Ikeja.
[caption id="attachment_7422" align="alignleft" width="2273"] L-R: Representative of Kick Against Indiscipline Corp Marshall, Mr. Eniola Adeniyi; Director Environmental Health Services, Onigbongbo Local Council Development Area, Sanitarian. Olalekan Emmanuel; Guest lecturer and Director Water Resources, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Oyedele James; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Education Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Monsurat Banire and Baale, Akinogun, Oregun, High Chief. Femi Akilo, during the year 2026 Coastal Community Advocacy Programme, held on 21st of October, 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
Gaji who spoke through the Director Environmental Education Unit, Mrs Monsurat Banire noted that flooding and improper waste management remained significant environmental challenges confronting coastal communities, threatening livelihoods, public health and the general well-being of residents.
Highlighting the theme “From Awareness to Action.” Gaji stressed that addressing these challenges required more than awareness campaigns, urging residents and other stakeholders to translate environmental knowledge into practical and sustained action.
He explained that Lagos, as a low-lying coastal state, was particularly vulnerable to flooding, a situation often aggravated by indiscriminate waste disposal, blocked drainage channels and waterways, poor sanitation practices and other human activities that impede the natural flow of water.
[caption id="attachment_7421" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Director Environmental Health Services, Onigbongbo Local Council Development Area, Sanitarian. Olalekan Emmanuel; Guest lecturer and Director Water Resources, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Oyedele James; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Education Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Monsurat Banire; Baale, Akinogun, Oregun, High Chief. Femi Akilo and Baale Wasimi, Onigbongbo, High Chief. Yisa Kehinde, during the year 2026 Coastal Community Advocacy Programme, held on 21st of October, 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
According to him, environmental advocacy must go beyond information dissemination to inspire behavioural change, empower residents with practical knowledge and promote a strong sense of shared responsibility for environmental protection.
He urged community members to keep drains and waterways free of waste, reduce the indiscriminate disposal of plastics and other refuse, observe proper sanitation practices and respond appropriately to flood early warnings.
The Permanent Secretary reaffirmed the commitment of the Lagos State Government, under the leadership of Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu, to addressing environmental challenges through sustained investments in drainage rehabilitation, flood mitigation, shoreline protection, waste management and community sensitisation.
He, however, emphasised that government interventions could only achieve lasting results when complemented by responsible actions at the grassroots, noting that community participation remained critical to building resilient and sustainable coastal settlements.
He called on market associations, artisans, community leaders and residents to take ownership of their immediate environment by discouraging indiscriminate dumping, preventing activities that obstruct drainage channels and waterways, and promoting proper waste disposal and sanitation practices.
The Permanent Secretary further urged participants to use the advocacy programme as an opportunity to become environmental change agents in their respective communities, encouraging them to influence others positively and sustain the message of environmental responsibility beyond the event.
He stressed that preventing flooding and safeguarding coastal communities required collective commitment, stronger grassroots participation, innovation and accountability from government, community organisations and individual residents.
[caption id="attachment_7420" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Representative of Kick Against Indiscipline Corp Marshall, Mr. Eniola Adeniyi; Director Environmental Health Services, Onigbongbo Local Council Development Area, Sanitarian. Olalekan Emmanuel; Guest lecturer and Director Water Resources, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Oyedele James; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Education Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Monsurat Banire and Baale, Akinogun, Oregun, High Chief. Femi Akilo, during the year 2026 Coastal Community Advocacy Programme, held on 21st of October, 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
He urged residents to take the message of “From Awareness to Action” into their homes, workplaces, markets and communities, emphasising that sustainable environmental management must become a daily responsibility rather than an occasional response to environmental challenges.
In his Lecture, the Guest Lecturer and Director of Water Resources, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Oyedele James, Emphasised a collective responsibility in waste management and environmental protection noting that everyone generates waste but often fails to take responsibility for its proper disposal.
He stressed that activities in upstream communities can adversely affect downstream areas, particularly coastal communities. He also emphasised the need to keep stormwater channels and their rights-of-way free from obstruction to ensure the free flow of water and reduce the risk of flooding.
He highlighted the importance of proactive community leadership, noting that timely preventive actions can avert potential disasters. He further described wetlands as natural retention areas for stormwater and filters for underground water, urging communities to protect these ecosystems and embrace responsible environmental practices to minimise flooding.
Kunle Adeshina
Director Public Affairs MOE&WR
21st October, 2026

title: LAGOS RESTATES ZERO TOLERANCE FOR BLOCKING ROADS, DRAINAGES WITH BUILDING MATERIALS
author: moel
excerpt:
.....As HC Env. leads officials on inpection tour of projects   
  
  
 Lagos State Government on Sunday restated it's zero tolerance for construction sites discharging or pla...
content:
.....As HC Env. leads officials on inpection tour of projects 
Lagos State Government on Sunday restated it's zero tolerance for construction sites discharging or placing materials on the roads and along drainage channels and prevalence of shanties along the Rights of Way, saying perpetrators will face the consequences.
Srate Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab restated the warning while leading state officials on inspection of some on-going projects in Central Lagos, LAWMA Transfer loading station at Simpson street and VGC in Ajah.
[caption id="attachment_7414" align="alignleft" width="1264"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji and his Counterparts in the Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Director Drainage Construction, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Dapo Ajadi and General Manager, Lagos Wastewater Management Office, Engr. Adefemi Afolabi, during a facility tour to Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Transfer Loading Station at Lagos Island, Lagos State October, 2026, on the 18th of October, 2026.[/caption]
In his words: "We have made it clear that construction sites responsible for these violations will be stopped and made to pay penalties for forcing the government to deploy resources to address their infractions"
He said the state will not relent in removing illegal structures wherever they spring up, urging media partners to come up with suggestions for stricter measures for carrying out removals if they have it.
"We have to keep carrying out these removals. If you have other suggestions for stricter measures, please share them with us. If you dont know the numbers, I can share them with you. We take people to court every day in this state, except Saturdays and Sundays. Every day, we take people to court"
He reiterated the belief of the present  administration that there must be consequences for bad behaviours. "That is our mantra. If we have regulations and laws, what distinguishes us from developed countries is our willingness to attach consequences to bad behaviour".
"People come into Lagos daily from different cultural backgrounds to settle here. That is why we have the Lagos State Residents Registration Agency (LASRRA) to register residents and enable us to account for them. However, when we push this narrative, some people accuse us of being elitist. It has become a chicken-and-egg situation: which comes first?", he explained.
[caption id="attachment_7417" align="alignleft" width="2400"] From left: Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji, his Counterpart in the Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite and other top officials from Lagos State Ministry of The Environment and Water Resources, during a drainage tour to Lagos Island, on the 18th of October, 2026.[/caption]
Speaking on LAWMA's readiness to tackle indiscriminate waste dumping,  he expressed the belief that  the roadmap towards achieving our vision as a state is on course.
He explained that the vision involves transitioning from a linear waste management system to one in which waste becomes a resource.
"We are almost there. The trucks have been shipped, while material recovery facilities and transfer loading stations are ongoing. If we already have one or two transfer loading stations in the state, what are we doing with them?", the Commissioner asked rhetorically.
The Commissioner said he led the officials to pay an unscheduled to the Simpson Transfer loading station to have a first experience of what is going on there.
He announced that unannounced visits will become a regular feature of the Ministry to its agencies.
He said during the visit to the Transfer loading station, the ministry was briefed by the Executive Director and head of operations were there furnished the state government with a roadmap and an update on the infrastructure.
[caption id="attachment_7416" align="alignleft" width="2400"] From left; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, his Counterpart in the Office of Environmental Services, Dr.Gaji Omobolaji and other top officials from Lagos State Ministry of The Environment and Water Resources, during a drainage tour to Lagos Island, Lagos State on the 18th of October, 2026.[/caption]
"These are some of the things we will be doing henceforth. We will be paying unannounced visits to managing directors of agencies under the ministry to ascertain what they are doing", Wahab added.
The team from the Ministry also returned to the area where it was working to regenerate Lagos Island and inspected the new infrastructure, checking the systems from Drop-in Extension 1 to 4.
"We also saw some of the equipment at work and gave instructions to ramp up preparations ahead of the next rainy season".
The team also paid a visit to the Victoria Garden City where petitions were received about about unusual flooding mlamd measures to address the challenge.
[caption id="attachment_7415" align="aligncenter" width="965"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji and his Counterparts in the Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu and General Manager, Lagos Wastewater Management Office, Engr. Adefemi Afolabi, during a facility tour to Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Transfer Loading Station at Lagos Island, Lagos State October, 2026, on the 18th of October, 2026.[/caption]
On the rehabilitation going on on the Lekki Epe Expressway,  Wahab urged residents to bear with the state through the inconvenience, adding that it is expected to be carried out in phases to minimise distruption to lives and properties.
Prominent among those who joined the Commissioner were the Special Adviser on the Environment,  Engr Kunle Rotimi- Akodu, Perm Secs, Environmental Services, Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen and Drainage Services, Engr Olakunle Adegbite, General Manager, LASWMO, Engr Femi Afolabi and Executive Secretary,  LAWRECO, Mrs Khadijat Adeyemo and directors from the Ministry.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director (Public Affairs)
MOE&WR
October 18, 2026

title: LAGOS, NCF SOUND CLIMATE ACTION ALARM.
author: moel
excerpt:
Sanwo-Olu Urges Lagos Residents to Protect Wetlands and Tackle Plastic Pollution as 20th Walk for Nature Holds at LASU, Ojo  
  
 The Lagos State Government and the Nigerian Co...
content:
Sanwo-Olu Urges Lagos Residents to Protect Wetlands and Tackle Plastic Pollution as 20th Walk for Nature Holds at LASU, Ojo
The Lagos State Government and the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF) on Saturday intensified calls for urgent climate action, commitment to environmental sustainability and climate resilience, asking residents to take urgent and collective action against plastic pollution and  degradation of natural ecosystems.
Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu made the call at the 20th edition of the annual Walk for Nature, organised by the Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources in partnership with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), held at Makanjuola Hall, Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo.
[caption id="attachment_7408" align="alignleft" width="2023"] L-R: Director General, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Dr. Joseph Onoja; Chairperson, Business Development & Communications Committee, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Mrs. Dame Marie Fatayi-Williams; Her Excellency, Former First Lady of Ogun State and Yeye Moremi Oodua Mrs. Olufunso Amosun, Chairman, National Executive Council, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Hon. Justice (Mrs.) R. I. B. Adebiyi; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji and Permanent Secretary, Office of Physical Planning, Mr. Olayinka Wasiu, during the 20th edition of the annual Walk For Nature exercise, held on the 17th of October, 2026, at Lagos State University (LASU),Ojo Lagos State.[/caption]
The Governor, who spoke through the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen  said the 20th edition provided an opportunity to reflect on the progress made in raising environmental awareness and renew the commitment to translating awareness into measurable environmental action.
Sanwo-Olu noted that Lagos generates approximately 13,000 tonnes of waste daily, with plastics accounting for about 15 per cent, expressing concern that improperly disposed plastic waste frequently finds its way into drains, canals and the lagoon, contributing to flooding and environmental pollution.
He described the challenge as one with direct implications for public health, homes, businesses and transportation, stressing that Lagos, as a coastal state with low-lying and densely populated communities, could not afford to delay action on climate change.
According to him, the state's wetlands, mangroves and lagoon fronts serve as natural defences against flooding and coastal erosion, warning that indiscriminate reclamation and development in these environmentally sensitive areas expose communities to greater risks.
[caption id="attachment_7407" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Director General, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Dr. Joseph Onoja; Chairperson, Business Development & Communications Committee, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Mrs. Dame Marie Fatayi-Williams; Her Excellency, Former First Lady of Ogun State and Yeye Moremi Oodua Mrs. Olufunso Amosun, Chairman, National Executive Council, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Hon. Justice (Mrs.) R. I. B. Adebiyi and Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji , during the 20th edition of the annual Walk For Nature exercise, held on the 17th of October, 2026, at Lagos State University (LASU),Ojo Lagos State.[/caption]
The Governor outlined government's interventions in three critical areas: plastic pollution control, the protection of wetlands and the expansion of drainage and green infrastructure.
On plastic pollution, he recalled the state's ban on Styrofoam and other specified single-use plastics, noting that enforcement commenced on July 1, 2025 adding that the government was also working with innovators to promote sustainable alternatives while strengthening environmental education in schools and communities.
Speaking on wetland protection, Sanwo-Olu stated that the government suspended reclamation activities on wetlands, floodplains and lagoon fronts without the requisite Environmental Impact Assessment approvals and drainage clearances in September 2025.
He emphasised that all development activities must comply with environmental regulations and drainage requirements, noting that the protection of wetlands and mangroves was essential to building a safer and more climate-resilient Lagos.
The Governor further reaffirmed the administration's commitment to investing in drainage infrastructure, restoring mangroves, planting trees and developing parks to strengthen the state's natural defences against flooding and rising temperatures.
Sanwo-Olu stressed that government efforts would achieve greater impact with the active participation of residents, urging them to dispose of waste responsibly, keep drains and drainage channels clear, reduce their reliance on single-use plastics and avoid building on wetlands and drainage corridors.
Addressing participants and students of Lagos State University at the exercise, he encouraged them to take the lead in promoting environmental responsibility within their hostels and surrounding communities through waste separation, tree planting and the adoption of sustainable practices.
He also urged young people to hold themselves, their communities and government accountable for protecting the environment, noting that their generation would bear the long-term consequences of decisions taken today.
The Governor commended the Nigerian Conservation Foundation for sustaining the Walk for Nature over the past two decades and acknowledged the contributions of the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, partners, volunteers and participants to the success of the initiative.
Sanwo-Olu urged participants to sustain the spirit of the exercise by making environmentally responsible choices in their daily lives, stressing that the success of the initiative would ultimately be measured by actions taken to protect the environment long after the walk has ended.
In his welcome address, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services,  Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, described the 20th edition of the Annual Walk for Nature as a significant milestone in Lagos State’s sustained advocacy for nature conservation, environmental awareness and responsible stewardship of natural resources.
Gaji represented by the director Ecology and Wetlands, Mrs Tolu Adeyo noted that the initiative has, over the past two decades, provided a vital platform for Government, conservation organisations, academia, the private sector, communities and young people to promote environmental sustainability.
Highlighting the theme, “Inspired for Climate Action – Lagos Must Listen, Our Action Matters,” Gaji stressed that climate change was no longer a distant concern, as its impacts were increasingly evident in rising temperatures, changing weather patterns, flooding and biodiversity loss.
He emphasised the importance of protecting and restoring natural ecosystems, particularly wetlands, mangroves, waterways, forests and green spaces, which serve as natural buffers against flooding, support biodiversity, store carbon and sustain community livelihoods.
[caption id="attachment_7406" align="alignleft" width="1213"] L-R: Director General, Nigeria Conservation Foundation (NCF) Dr. Joseph Onoja; Her Excellency, Former First Lady of Ogun State and Yeye Moremi Oodua Mrs. Olufunso Amosun; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji and Permanent Secretary, Office of Physical Planning, Mr. Olayinka Wasiu and during the 20th edition of the annual Walk For Nature exercise, held on the 17th of October, 2026, at Lagos State University (LASU),Ojo Lagos State.[/caption]
He called on residents, businesses, communities and institutions to translate environmental awareness into practical action, stressing that climate resilience could not be achieved by Government alone.
Also speaking, the Chairman of the NEC of the NCF, Justice R I B Adebiyi described the climate crisis is a test of man's responsibility, his creativity, courage, and our common humanity.
"Future generations may never know our names, but they will live with the consequences of the decisions we make today. They will either inherit a world in which we ignored the warning signs, or a world in which we dared to respond".
"Let them inherit a world of hope rather than regret, a world of opportunity rather than destruction, she explained.
The 20th Walk for Nature forms part of ongoing efforts to mobilise residents, particularly young people, around environmental conservation, climate action and the protection of Lagos State's natural ecosystems.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina,
Director, Public Affairs
Ministry of Environment and Water Resources (MOE&WR)
17th October, 2026

title: SANITATION MUST BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE DAILY OPERATIONS, CULTURE OF EVERY SCHOOL -LASG
author: moel
excerpt:
As State holds Grand Finale of Secondary Schools Sanitation Competition
 
 

Lagos State Government on Tuesday stated that going forward  Sanitation must become an integral pa...
content:
As State holds Grand Finale of Secondary Schools Sanitation Competition
Lagos State Government on Tuesday stated that going forward  Sanitation must become an integral part of the daily operations and culture of every school and not limited to special occasions, inspection periods, or competition days. The charge was given by the Special Adviser to the Governor on the Environment,  Engr Kunle Rotimi-Akodu during the 2026 Lagos State Secondary Schools Sanitation Competition and Awards ceremony held at the LCCI Conference Centre, Alausa. [caption id="attachment_7400" align="alignleft" width="1080"] L-R: Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Basic & Secondary Education Mr. Adesina Oluyemi: Representative of the Special Adviser on Environment and Director Climate Change, Office of Environmental Services, Mr. Micheal Bankole: Rep of the DG, Office of Education Quantity Assurance (OEQA) and
Director Planning, Research and Statistics, Mrs. Evelyn Pelemo and the Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Environmental Services, Dr.Hassan Sanuth, during the 2026 Lagos State Secondary School Sanitation Award ceremony, held on the 13th of October 2026, at Lagos State Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Nurudeem Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja Lagos State.[/caption] Akodu who spoke through the Director Climate Change and Environmental Planning, Mr Bankole Michael said School administrators should ensure that sanitation facilities are regularly inspected and maintained while teachers should continue to educate and guide students on environmental responsibility. Parents and guardians, according to him, should also reinforce these values at home while students take ownership of their surroundings by keeping classrooms clean, avoiding littering, conserving water, and participating in appropriate environmental initiatives. He reiterated that achieving sustainable improvements in school sanitation requires more than government intervention, maintaining that School administrators, teachers, students, parents, guardians, corporate organizations, non-governmental organizations, and community groups all have important roles to play. [caption id="attachment_7403" align="alignleft" width="1080"] Winners of the 2026 Lagos State Secondary Schools Sanitation Competition and Award Ceremony for Day school and Model Colleges categories, Model Senior College, Ikorodu and Government Senior College, Ipaja in a group photograph with the representatives of the Special Adviser on Environment and Director Climate Change, Mr. Micheal Bankole, during the 2026 Lagos State Secondary Schools Sanitation Award Ceremony, held on 13th of October 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Nurudeen Olowopopo drive Alausa Ikeja Lagos State.[/caption] "It is through collective responsibility, effective collaboration, and sustained commitment that we can establish and maintain acceptable sanitation standards in our schools", he maintained. Akodu commended the improvement observed during the sanitatiom assessment exercise across the schools, saying during the Year 2024 exercise, the ministry recorded 65%, while there has been a marked improvement by all the participating schools for the 2026 exercise. [caption id="attachment_7402" align="alignleft" width="686"] L-R: , Representatives of the Special Adviser on Environment and Director Climate Change, Mr. Micheal Bankole, presenting a 1st place award on Sanitation and Hygiene best practices (Model College Category) to Lagos State Model Senior College, Ikorodu, Lagos State, during the 2026 Lagos State Secondary School Sanitation Award ceremony, held on the 13th of October 2026, at Lagos State Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Nurudeem Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja Lagos State.[/caption] He used the occasion to implore  all concerned authorities to ensure that the renewed passion is experienced in all public schools and not necessarily the schools nominated for the competition, saying: "It must become an integral part of the daily operations and culture of every school". The Special Adviser also called on every stakeholder to regard sanitation as a shared responsibility and a practical investment in the health, dignity, safety, and future of our children. In his words: "Together, we must ensure that every child in Lagos State has the opportunity to learn in an environment that is clean, safe, healthy, and conducive to academic excellence". "As we celebrate the participating schools and students, let the knowledge gained and lessons learnt through this competition translate into practical actions that will improve sanitation standards across our schools". Earlier, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen said the event represents an opportunity to celebrate the achievements of schools with exceptional commitment to cleanliness, hygiene and environmental responsibility; both within their learning environments and more importantly in shaping the habits, values and attitudes of young people Gaji who was represented by the Director Sanitation Services,  Dr Hassan Sanuth stated that the initiative offers students an opportunity to showcase their ingenuity through environmental sustainability projects, upcycling, and environmental awareness campaigns. Gaji went on to say the activities such as the competitionencourage young people to think creatively, take initiative, and contribute meaningfully to solving environmental challenges in their schools and communities. [caption id="attachment_7401" align="alignleft" width="1367"] From left: Representative of the Special Adviser on Environment and Director Climate Change, Office of Environmental Services, Mr.Micheal Bankole, presenting a 1st place winner for Award of Sanitation and Hygiene Best Practices (Day School Category) to Government Senior College, Ipaja, during the 2026 Lagos State Secondary School Sanitation Award ceremony, held on the 13th of October 2026, at Lagos State Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Nurudeem Olowopopo drive, Alausa Ikeja Lagos State.[/caption] The highlight of the event was the presentation  of award to the best school in the day school category and model school category for Sanitation and hygiene best practices as well as first and second runners up alongside individual awards. Government Senior College, Ipaja came first in the Day School category while Government Junior Model College emerged winners in the Model College category attracting a plaque and prizes that include 1000L Geepee Tank, 1nos. Black Wheeler Bin and Waste bags. title: LASG TAKES WASTE MANAGEMENT EDUCATION TO NEXT LEVEL THROUGH PRACTICAL KNOWLEDGE SHARING.
author: moel
excerpt: The Lagos State Government on Wednesday reaffirmed its commitment to entrenching sustainable waste management practices in schools across Lagos State through practical knowledge t...
content:
The Lagos State Government on Wednesday reaffirmed its commitment to entrenching sustainable waste management practices in schools across Lagos State through practical knowledge to reduce, reuse, recover and properly manage waste.
The commitment was reiterated at the 2026 Environmental Bees Club Handlers’ Symposium, themed “Effective Waste Management Audit for Zero-Waste Schools: Waste Characterisation and Circular Economy.”
Speaking at the symposium, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji  emphasised that effective waste management in schools must go beyond maintaining clean surroundings to understanding the nature, quantity and sources of waste generated.
Gaji, represented by the Director Environmental Education Unit, Mrs Monsurat Banire  emphasised that effective waste management in schools must go beyond maintaining clean surroundings to understanding the nature, quantity and sources of waste generated.
He explained that  audits and characterisation provide schools with the necessary evidence to identify materials that could be reused, recovered, recycled or appropriately disposed noting that such an approach would help schools develop practical and sustainable waste management systems.
According to him, the Environmental Bees Club has continued to serve as an important platform for inculcating sound environmental practices among students, recalling that teachers were exposed to practical urban, school and home gardening activities in 2024, while the 2025 edition focused on composting, waste-to-wealth initiatives and other productive uses of discarded materials.
The Permanent Secretary also disclosed that over 200 schools participated in the Lagos State Government-UNICEF plastic collection competition, through which Lagos State contributed more than one-third of Nigeria’s plastic recycling target.
He urged Environmental Bees Club handlers to transform waste management into an active learning experience for students by using waste audits to teach observation and data collection, waste characterisation to promote classification and analysis, and reuse and recovery initiatives to develop problem-solving skills.
Gaji stressed the importance of making the concept of circular economy practical and relatable to students, encouraging them to look beyond the disposal of waste and consider the value that could still be recovered from materials after their initial use.
“Our responsibility is not merely to teach students where waste should be disposed of, but to encourage them to ask why the waste was generated in the first place, whether it could have been avoided, and what value can still be recovered from it.” he said.
[caption id="attachment_7391" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Founder, FABE International, Mrs. Temitope Okunnu; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Education Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Monsurat Banire; Founder, Project Save the Planet, Mr. Benjamin Suleiman; Director in the Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Olaleye Esther and Director Sanitation Services, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Hassan Sanuth, during the annual Environmental BEES CLUB Handlers Symposium, held on the 7th of October, 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry building(LCCI) Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
He further urged the handlers to take the lessons and knowledge acquired at the symposium back to their respective schools and strengthen environmental education through practical activities that would encourage responsible waste management among students.
The Permanent Secretary commended the facilitators and Environmental Bees Club handlers for their commitment to the programme saying that the vision of achieving zero-waste schools could only be realised through sustained practical learning.
[caption id="attachment_7390" align="alignleft" width="1861"] L-R: Founder, FABE International, Mrs. Temitope Okunnu; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Education Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Monsurat Banire; Founder, Project Save the Planet, Mr. Benjamin Suleiman; Director Sanitation Services, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Hassan Sanuth and Director in the Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Omolara Brown, during the annual Environmental BEES CLUB Handlers Symposium, held on the 7th of October, 2026, at Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry building(LCCI) Nurudeen Olowopopo drive, Ikeja, Lagos State.[/caption]
He mentioned that such forum is effective in making responsible environmental decisions and habits that students would carry from their schools into their homes and communities.
He expressed confidence that continued collaboration among the government, schools, teachers and students would strengthen Lagos State’s efforts to promote a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable environment.
In his Lecture by the guest lecturer, Ambassador Phillips Obuesi, he emphasized that waste characterization is different from waste auditing, stressing the need for school waste handlers to understand where different categories of waste are generated within their schools.
He explained that proper characterization would enable handlers to identify the sources and types of waste generated at various locations, track waste effectively, and develop appropriate strategies for managing them.
Ambassador Obuesi also highlighted the importance of proper management of hazardous waste in schools, stressing that such waste must be handled carefully and, where necessary, appropriate authorities should be contacted for safe evacuation and disposal.
He advocated for waste separation at source, noting that students must be adequately educated on the different types of waste they generate and how to handle them responsibly.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director Public Affairs
MOE&WR
7th October, 2026

title: LAGOS STATE STATE GOVERNMENT MINISTRY OF THE ENVIRONMENT & WATER RESOURCESPUBLIC AFFAIRS UNIT
author: moel
excerpt:
YOUR CRITICISMS OF OUR WASTE MANAGEMENT, FLASH FLOOD PREVENTION MEASURES ARE MISLEADING-LASG 
  
 Lagos State Government on Tuesday described as misleading, criticisms tha...
content:
YOUR CRITICISMS OF OUR WASTE MANAGEMENT, FLASH FLOOD PREVENTION MEASURES ARE MISLEADING-LASG
Lagos State Government on Tuesday described as misleading, criticisms that the state has no plans for waste management beyond clearing refuse after it accumulates and that flooding issues are being ignored.
Responding to erroneous assertions on the State waste management measures and flash flooding issues by a governorship candidate in the 2027 elections during a recent popular TV programme, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab asserted that it is vital to distinguish between identifying challenges and acknowledging the concrete efforts being made to address them.
“Beyond emergency interventions, Lagos is investing in Modern Transfer Loading Stations, Material Recovery Facilities, recycling, composting and the Epe waste-to-energy project. The objective is to transition from decades of pick-and-dump practices to a sustainable system where waste becomes a resource for energy and economic value”, Wahab stressed.
The Commissioner reiterated that Lagos generates an estimated 13,000–15,000 tonnes of municipal waste daily and that  in May 2026 alone, LAWMA and PSP operators evacuated approximately 418,500 tonnes, averaging 13,200 tonnes daily, stressing that the growing volume is partly driven by Lagos’ expanding population and daily influx of people into the state.
He explained that the figures underscore the enormous scale of the responsibility of the state and do not suggest that every resident receives satisfactory service. “We acknowledge collection failures, underperforming PSP operators and operational bottlenecks”.
The Commissioner described Waste management is an interconnected system saying delays at disposal facilities affect truck turnaround, disrupt collection schedules and eventually create refuse accumulation across neighbourhoods. “At Olusosun, rehabilitation of Road E and additional disposal platforms increased operational efficiency. Truck movements across disposal facilities rose to 1,866 in the week following the intervention, while Olusosun recorded an increase from 574 to 1,012 trips”
He emphasized that the state is strengthening property enumeration, geocoded service locations, GPS tracking, weighbridge measurements, collection records and recovery data whilst also reforming the PSP system, sanctioning and terminating operators where necessary.
“On data transparency, the principle is straightforward: a modern waste management system must measure what it manages”, he stated.
Wahab admitted that Lagos has significant work ahead which it honestly acknowledges, but to suggest that nothing is being done ignores the investments, infrastructure and operational reforms already underway.
The Commissioner stated that the monthly environmental sanitation exercise is not a substitute for an effective waste management system and that any genuine conversation should therefore move beyond describing Lagos as “stinky” and focus on measurable outcomes: tonnes collected, routes completed, missed collections, complaint resolution, recurring blackspots and waste diverted from landfills.
According to Wahab, there are some fundamental questions  the state is answering with measurable performance like: “Does every household have an assigned waste collector?, is the operator adequately equipped to deliver the service?, was the scheduled collection route completed?, when residents complain, does anyone respond?, is collected waste properly treated, recovered or disposed of?, why should emergency evacuation become a substitute for reliable daily collection?
On the criticism of the state flood prevention measures, Wahab informed that Lagos has invested in drainage infrastructure, pump stations, year-round maintenance, flood abatement operations, ban on styrofoam and single-use plastics, wetland preservation and the removal of structures on floodplains. Many of which the Governorship candidate criticized and attacked the government for.
Wahab affirmed that the interventions have reportedly reduced flooding incidents by 75–80% statewide asserting that It is therefore misleading to suggest that flooding is being ignored or that no meaningful progress has been made.
He said any such criticism must be viewed against the realities of Lagos’ coastal geography, tidal locks and the growing impact of climate change, adding every critic should appreciate that even the most resilient drainage infrastructure cannot entirely eliminate flash flooding in a coastal megacity.
“While challenges remain, the evidence of sustained interventions must form part of the conversation. Flooding is a global coastal challenge, not one peculiar to Lagos. Amsterdam, Thailand, Nepal, Afghanistan (despite having a dry land), even the almighty USA.  Criticism should be informed by geography, climate realities and the progress already recorded, not political rhetoric”, he opined.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director, Public Affairs
MOE&WR
September 30, 2026

title: LAGOS DIRECTS IMMEDIATE RELOCATION OF RESIDENTS IN FLOOD-PRONE AREAS TO HIGHER GROUNDS
author: moel
excerpt:
NIHSA Issues Seven-Day Flood Alert for Lagos: Eti-Osa, Lagos Island, Ajah and Other Areas at Risk  
Residents are urged to take flood warnings seriously as rising river l...
content:
NIHSA Issues Seven-Day Flood Alert for Lagos: Eti-Osa, Lagos Island, Ajah and Other Areas at Risk

Residents are urged to take flood warnings seriously as rising river levels threaten vulnerable communities across the state.
Following a new seven-day flood alert advisory (NFA-2026-2022) issued over the weekend by the Nigerian Hydrological Services Agency (NiHSA), which affects Lagos and 14 other states, the Lagos State Government has directed the immediate evacuation of residents living in low-lying and flood-prone communities to prevent loss of lives and damage to property.
In a statement issued on Sunday evening, the Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr Tokunbo Wahab, listed areas identified as vulnerable to flooding. These include Eti-Osa, Lagos Island Local Government Area, Oke-Ira Nla (Ajah), Kirikiri (Sea Port), Ilaje Waterfront Jetty, and Jetty Terminal B, among others.
According to the Commissioner, the State Government is treating the advisory with the utmost seriousness and has intensified monitoring activities across the identified locations, as well as other riverine, low-lying, and flood-prone communities.
Wahab urged residents in vulnerable areas not to disregard the warning or wait until floodwaters rise before taking action, stressing that early preparation and temporary relocation to safer areas could prevent avoidable tragedies.
He reiterated that residents of flood-prone communities should move to higher ground and remain there until the peak of the resurgent rainy season has passed.
“We are urging Lagosians, particularly those living in flood-prone and low-lying areas, not to take this warning lightly. When the signs point to danger, the safest decision is to move early. No property is worth risking a life,” Wahab stated.
He noted that Lagos typically experiences a second phase of the rainy season from September, characterised by increased rainfall, rising water levels, and tidal influences that can exacerbate flooding in vulnerable locations.
The Commissioner therefore advised residents living near rivers, lagoons, wetlands, drainage channels, and other water bodies to remain vigilant and comply with all safety advisories issued by relevant government agencies.
Wahab specifically called on communities situated along the Ogun River and other major waterways to exercise heightened caution, noting that upstream rainfall intensity and water levels in connected river systems could significantly affect downstream conditions in Lagos.
He also urged residents of low-lying areas and riverbank communities, including Isheri North, Kara, Itowolo, Ajegunle, Majidun, Ogolonto, parts of Agboyi, and other settlements downstream of Isheri Olofin, to remain on high alert during the period 19 to 25 September.
The Commissioner further advised residents across the state, particularly those in coastal and waterfront communities, to closely monitor official flood forecasts and be prepared to relocate temporarily whenever flooding becomes imminent.
According to the NiHSA report, rising river levels could result in flooding across vulnerable communities and impact critical facilities such as schools, healthcare centres, markets, farms, and places of worship.
Wahab therefore called on affected local governments, emergency management agencies, community leaders, and residents to activate early warning and response mechanisms, while ensuring that people, livestock, and valuable possessions are moved to safer locations where necessary.
He stated that the Lagos State Government would continue to monitor river levels, rainfall patterns, and other hydrological developments in collaboration with relevant federal agencies.
He added that routine cleaning, maintenance, and monitoring of drainage infrastructure across the state would also be sustained.
The Commissioner appealed to residents to support the government's flood mitigation efforts by refraining from indiscriminate dumping of refuse into drains, canals, and waterways, noting that blocked drainage channels can worsen flooding and delay the recession of floodwaters.
He also cautioned residents against walking or driving through flooded roads, bridges, and fast-moving water, urging those in vulnerable areas to make arrangements for temporary relocation whenever official warnings indicate an imminent threat.
Wahab stressed that the protection of lives and property remains the government's foremost priority and urged Lagosians to treat flood forecasts as critical safety information requiring immediate action.
He assured residents that the State Government would continue to deploy all necessary measures to reduce flood risks and provide timely updates as the situation evolves.
He further urged Lagosians to remain calm, vigilant, and responsive to official advisories.Signed Kunle Adeshina Director, Public Affairs Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MOE&WR) 21 September 2026.

title: LAGOS TO GET OVER 200 NEW COMPACTOR TRUCKS TO IMPROVE WASTE EVACUATION
author: moel
excerpt: ....As Deputy Governor Kadri Hamzat leads wife, Oluremi, HOS, HC Env, SA Env. other officials to monitor sanitation in Festac & Bariga The Lagos State Government is set to take delivery of over 200 new compactor truc...
content:
....As Deputy Governor Kadri Hamzat leads wife, Oluremi, HOS, HC Env, SA Env. other officials to monitor sanitation in Festac & Bariga

The Lagos State Government is set to take delivery of over 200 new compactor trucks as part of measures to strengthen waste collection and evacuation across the State.

The Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, disclosed this on Saturday while leading his wife, Oluremi Hamzat, and other top government officials to monitor the August monthly environmental sanitation exercise in the Amuwo-Odofin Local Government Area.

Speaking to journalists in Festac Town after participating in the cleaning exercise, Hamzat urged residents to desist from patronising unregistered cart pushers and instead ensure that their waste is handed over to registered Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators.

He said residents have an important role to play in ensuring that waste does not end up in unauthorised locations, particularly drainage channels and canals, which could contribute to flooding.

“What we need our people to also do is to make sure that they patronise their PSP, not the cart pushers. Because those ones are not organised. You don't know where it is ending up. But the PSP will take it to the landfills. The cart pushers, we don't know. It might even be in the canals.”

Hamzat added that residents' cooperation was essential to preventing indiscriminate waste disposal and protecting the environment.

“That's the encouragement that we're giving our citizens—to make sure that you play your role and ensure that the garbage doesn't end up in a canal and therefore lead to flooding,” he said.

The Deputy Governor described the monthly environmental sanitation exercise as an important initiative aimed at promoting a culture of environmental responsibility among residents.

According to him, maintaining a healthy environment requires the collective participation of government and citizens.

“We cannot be a people without a healthy environment,” he said.

[caption id="attachment_7377" align="alignleft" width="1536"] Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, (third right), Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab (Second right) with them are staff of Amuwo Odofin Local Government and School Pupils, during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7376" align="alignleft" width="1536"] L-R: Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat: Chairman, Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Prince Lanre Sanusi and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab,
during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7375" align="alignleft" width="1264"] From left: Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat: Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab: Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat and the Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu (right), during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7374" align="alignleft" width="1264"] L:R : Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption]

Government Intensifies Efforts to Address Waste on Medians

Also speaking during the exercise on measures to address the accumulation of waste on road medians, the Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, who was accompanied by the Special Adviser on the Environment, Engr. Kunle Rotimi-Akodu, said the situation was gradually improving.

Wahab disclosed that the Ministry had established emergency response teams operating 24 hours daily to address environmental challenges, while efforts were also ongoing to improve landfill and dumpsite infrastructure across the State.

He said the Ministry would continue to engage PSP waste operators while intervening where necessary to improve their operational capacity and service delivery.

The Commissioner expressed optimism that improved waste collection services would encourage more residents to pay their waste bills, thereby strengthening the financial sustainability of PSP operations.

On measures to curb the activities of cart pushers, Wahab said the Government was engaging with them but stressed that any solution adopted must take into consideration the long-term environmental and security implications.

He said:

“We don't want to say because we're in a situation, we take steps that will come to harm us later in life. Most of these cart pushers, ask yourself, where is the waste usually dumped? Drainage, medians and so on.”

The Commissioner further noted that security findings had raised concerns about the involvement of some cart pushers in other criminal activities.

“In addition to that, security findings have also shown that some of them are part of those gangs involved in cutting metals and doing all sorts. We can't go that route,” Wahab reiterated.

HOS Urges Residents to Make Cleanliness an Everyday Responsibility

Meanwhile, the Head of Service, Mr. Olabode Agoro, who led another team of government officials to Bariga LCDA to monitor the exercise, urged residents to take greater responsibility for the cleanliness of their surroundings.

He also warned that individuals and establishments found violating environmental laws would face appropriate sanctions.

Agoro, who was represented by the Permanent Secretary, Public Service Office, Mrs. Sunkanmi Oyegbola, stressed that government alone could not achieve a cleaner and healthier Lagos without the active participation and cooperation of residents.

He said government officials were participating in the sanitation exercise to lead by example and encourage residents to embrace environmental cleanliness as a collective responsibility.

The Head of Service urged residents not to wait until the last Saturday of the month before cleaning their surroundings, but to make environmental cleanliness an everyday practice.

“We are here to ensure that the environment is clean and to encourage citizens to come out and clean their surroundings. Government has declared this day for residents to participate in environmental sanitation, and we are here to lead by example and encourage everyone to join us,” he said.

Prominent among government officials who participated in the monitoring exercise across the locations were the Commissioner for Special Duties and Intergovernmental Relations, Mr. Gbenga Oyerinde; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Mr. Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen; Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Olakunle Adegbite; other Permanent Secretaries; Local Government Chairmen; heads of government agencies; and members of the Committee of Wives of Lagos State Officials (COWLSO).

Signed

Kunle Adeshina Director, Public Affairs Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources

29 August 2026

title: LAGOS SEEKS STRONGER REGULATION, COLLABORATION WITH WASTE MANAGERS TO IMPROVE WASTE DISPOSAL
author: moel
excerpt: The Lagos State Government has reiterated its commitment to strengthening the regulation of Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and improving waste collection, transportation and disposal across the State. The C...
content:
The Lagos State Government has reiterated its commitment to strengthening the regulation of Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and improving waste collection, transportation and disposal across the State.

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, stated this on Wednesday during a meeting with the executive members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria (AWAMN), held as part of ongoing efforts to address operational challenges affecting the State’s waste management system.

The meeting provided an opportunity for the Government and waste management operators to review developments across the waste management value chain, with particular attention to the condition of dumpsites, challenges confronting PSP operators and measures required to improve operational efficiency and reduce turnaround time for waste collection and disposal.

[caption id="attachment_7370" align="alignleft" width="1280"] (1). L-R. The Secretary General of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria (AWAMN) Mr Taiye Kolade, The President of the Association Waste Managers of Nigeria ( AWAMN) Dr Olugbega Adebola, and the Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, during a stakeholder meeting with Executive Members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria held in Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources conference room on the 27th of August, 2026.[/caption]

Wahab stressed the need for all stakeholders in the sector to work towards a common objective of establishing an effective, efficient and sustainable waste management system in Lagos. He noted that the Government would continue to engage operators to identify challenges and develop practical solutions.

While acknowledging recent improvements at landfill sites across the State, the Commissioner emphasised the need for further interventions to make the facilities fully functional, efficient and sustainable.

[caption id="attachment_7369" align="alignleft" width="1280"] The Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and water Resource Mr Tokunbo Wahab, The Permanent Secretary Office of the Drainage Service and water Resources Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, Executive Director LAWMA, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, during a stakeholder meeting with the Executive Members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria held in Ministry of the Environment and water Resources Conference room on the 27th of August, 2026.[/caption]

He also reiterated the importance of providing proper access roads, drainage systems, operational platforms and other essential facilities to facilitate the smooth movement of waste trucks within the dumpsites.

According to him, ongoing improvements at the Solous dumpsite would significantly reduce pressure on other disposal locations, particularly those serving Alimosho, Ikotun-Ejigbo, Ayobo and surrounding communities. He added that the improvements would also reduce turnaround time for PSP operators and enable them to provide more efficient services to residents.

The Commissioner further disclosed that the State Government was exploring measures to improve the financial sustainability of PSP operations, including cost recovery mechanisms and appropriate adjustments that would enable operators to deliver their services more effectively.

He, however, stressed that improved financial arrangements must be matched by accountability, transparency and effective service delivery.

“No PSP operator should use the challenges at the dumpsites or other operational difficulties as an excuse for failing to provide the required services to residents,” he said.

Wahab called on AWAMN to strengthen its internal regulatory mechanisms and ensure that every PSP operator fulfils its contractual obligations, maintains its fleet and provides consistent waste collection services within its assigned areas.

He also expressed support for the association’s proposal to have environmental officers attached to wards across the State to monitor waste management activities at the community level.

He explained that the officers would help ensure that household waste is properly collected, payments for waste services are made, PSP operators perform efficiently and residents receive continuous sensitisation on proper waste disposal practices.

Wahab also stressed that effective enforcement would be critical to ensuring that residents patronise designated PSP operators and desist from indiscriminate disposal of waste on roads and other unauthorised locations.

He urged AWAMN to submit its recommendations on sustainable waste management for further consideration by the State Government. The proposals are expected to cover enforcement, cost recovery, waste treatment and disposal, as well as the regulation of PSP operators.

AWAMN Commends Lagos Government

Responding, the President of AWAMN, Dr. Olugbenga Adebola, commended the Ministry and its leadership for their commitment and personal intervention in addressing challenges within the waste management sector.

Adebola said the association had responded to the Government’s directives by inspecting disposal sites and engaging contractors to undertake improvement works at some dumpsite locations.

He disclosed that the association had also worked with officials of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) to identify infrastructure and operational requirements at the various dumpsites.

According to him, some access roads had been opened and improved, while further work, including stone-base reinforcement, was required to ensure that the roads remain functional during the rainy season and can withstand the weight of heavy waste trucks.

The AWAMN President also called for increased attention to the management and maintenance of disposal facilities, noting that adequate operational platforms and equipment were essential to improving turnaround time and preventing unnecessary delays for waste trucks.

Adebola further disclosed that the association had established a dumpsite committee to work with relevant government agencies in monitoring activities at disposal facilities and developing solutions to identified operational challenges.

On PSP operations, Adebola said the association was ready to collaborate with the State Government in developing a comprehensive and sustainable waste management framework that would go beyond waste collection and transportation to encompass disposal, waste treatment, enforcement and cost recovery.

Present at the meeting were the Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Executive Director, Finance, LAWMA, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi; and Directors in the Ministry.

Signed

Adekunle Adeshina Director, Public Affairs Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources

27 August 2026

title: LASG SEEKS, GETS  COMMUNITIES BUY-IN TO COMMENCE WORK ON MATERIAL RECOVERY FACILITY (MRF) AT AGBOWA
author: moel
excerpt: The Lagos State Government on Monday engaged the traditional rulers and leaders of the Owu Ikosi and Agbowa Ikosi communities on the need to collaborate and ensure the early commencement of work on a proposed Material Re...
content:
The Lagos State Government on Monday engaged the traditional rulers and leaders of the Owu Ikosi and Agbowa Ikosi communities on the need to collaborate and ensure the early commencement of work on a proposed Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Agbowa in the Epe division.
This is just as the traditional rulers, the Abowa of Agbowa Ikosi, Oba Owolabi Momson and the Olowu of Owu Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari gave a commitment on behalf of their communities for the State government to commence work on the proposed project right away.
Speaking during a meeting with the traditional rulers and chiefs of the two communities, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, stressed the need for broad-based community acceptance and ownership of the project by the two communities to prevent any form of disagreement.
Wahab explained that the proposed MRF should be viewed as a major development initiative rather than merely a waste recovery facility, noting that the Lagos State Government had been deliberate in spreading critical infrastructure and development projects across the State.
The Commissioner noted that the meeting was convened to resolve outstanding concerns and ensure that all parties were adequately carried along before the State proceeds with the project.
[caption id="attachment_7366" align="alignleft" width="1280"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr Kamar Olowosago, Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, Honorable Commissioner, for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, Director from the Surveyor General's Office, Surv O. Ogunbiyi, Acting Surveyor General, Mr Odupe Olalekan, Managing Director LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin during a stakeholders meeting held in Ministry of the Environment Conference room on the 24Th of August, 2026.[/caption]
According to him, while the State has a mandate to deliver sustainable waste management infrastructure, it is equally committed to ensuring that communities hosting such projects understand, accept and ultimately take ownership of them.
“It is a major development we are bringing to that site, and we have been very deliberate about how we spread development across the State; this meeting is to resolve whatever the issues are. We have to be frank because we do not want to make any mistake,” he said.
[caption id="attachment_7365" align="alignleft" width="1080"] The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr Kamar Olowoshago, Abowa of Agbowa Ikosi, Oba Saheed Momson, Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, Olowu of Owu Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari, Executive Director Finance LAWMA, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Service and Water Resources, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, Ag. Surveyor General, Mr Odupe Olalekan, Director from the Surveyor General's Office, Surv. O. Ogunbiyi, and the Managing Director LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin during a stakeholders meeting held in Ministry of the Environment Conference room on the 24th of August, 2026.[/caption]
The Commissioner subsequently reaffirmed the State Government’s commitment to ensuring that both communities are fully carried along, with the traditional institutions and relevant government agencies working together to resolve any issues that may arise in the course of the project.
He stressed that no side would be favoured at the expense of the other, adding that the objective was to achieve an arrangement that would promote development while respecting the interests of the two communities.
Wahab, acknowledging the role of the two traditional rulers, the Abowa of Agbowa-Ikosi, Oba Saheed Momson, and the Olowu of Owu-Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari, in helping to resolve the concerns, noted that their willingness to see the “bigger picture” and prioritise the development of the area was very commendable.
Wahab further assured the stakeholders that the concerns raised by the traditional institutions and community representatives would be given due consideration, stressing that the State Government would not impose the project without carrying the affected communities along.
The Commissioner said the State Government would ensure that the agreed positions from the meeting were formally documented through correspondence to all stakeholders, providing a clear framework for subsequent actions.
He assured the stakeholders that the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, the Lagos State Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), the Ministry of Physical Planning and Urban Development, the Lands Bureau, the consultants and other relevant agencies would continue to work together to achieve success on the project.
Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr. Kamar Olowoshago, expressed appreciation to the traditional rulers, chiefs, community leaders and other stakeholders for their constructive engagement, saying it is to his delight that work can now commence on the Agbowa, Epe location just as it has started in the Erekiti location in Badagry.
The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, stated that the proposed Material Recovery Facility is expected to strengthen waste recovery, recycling and resource utilisation while supporting the State Government’s efforts to reduce the volume of waste ultimately disposed of at landfills.
He reiterated that the administration of Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu remained committed to implementing sustainable environmental solutions across Lagos, while ensuring that communities are active partners in projects that directly affect them.
Responding jointly, the Olowu of Owu-Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari and  the Abowa of Agbowa- Ikosi, Oba Owolabi Momson jointly   expressed their support for development initiative that would improve the communities, while urging the State Government to ensure that all relevant stakeholders are properly consulted and carried along.
They explained that the communities were not opposed to development, saying the presentation of the project and its proposed facilities was satisfactory.
 He added that the state government must ensure that all components contained in the project plan are fully implemented.
Also present at the meeting were Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; and the Acting Surveyor-General of Lagos State, Surv. Olalekan Odupe.
Others included the Managing Director of LAWMA, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin; Executive Director, Finance, LAWMA, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi; as well as other top officials in the Ministry.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina

title: SANWO -OLU WIFE URGES RESIDENTS TO MAKE CLEANINESS OF THE ENVIRONMENT, A DAILY AFFAIR
author: moel
excerpt: ...Exercise Monitored in Ibeju-Lekki by Deputy Governor's Wife, Environment Commissioner; SA Environment Leads Badagry Team The First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke-Sanwo-Olu, on Saturday urged all residents n...
content:
...Exercise Monitored in Ibeju-Lekki by Deputy Governor's Wife, Environment Commissioner; SA Environment Leads Badagry Team
The First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke-Sanwo-Olu, on Saturday urged all residents not to wait till the last Saturday of the month to embark on the cleaning of their environment but make it an everyday affair.
The First Lady spoke at Eputu 'London' in Ibeju- Lekki Local Government when she monitored the July edition of the sanitation exercise alongside the wife of the Deputy Governor, Mrs Oluremi Hamzat, and Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr Tokunbo Wahab, and selected Permanent Secretaries and top officials of the State.
Dr Sanwo-Olu expressed appreciation to the residents of Eputu 'London' who came out in their large numbers to participate in the exercise,saying: "We are very, very proud of our people. We noticed today that in Ebutu London, both the children and the parents came out very early to clean their environment"
"Even though we are noticing that we have all the floods and things happening in Lagos State, we are making a conscious effort to create awareness among our people to ensure that they remove all the debris as much as possible", she stated.
While describing the participation of people as a work in progress, the First Lady said that explains why school pupils are being involved so that the message of cleanliness can be imbibed at a younger age.
She added that this would ensure that whatever is handed down over to them, they will continue with it as they grow into adulthood.
Dr Sanwo-Olu gave a commitment that from the August edition, students of tertiary institutions will also form a part of the monitoring of the monthly sanitation exercise.
[caption id="attachment_7361" align="alignleft" width="2170"] L-R: Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Olori Ogunfolu Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, Her Royal Majesty, Afolashade Ojuolape Idogun; Chairman, Ibeju-Lekki Local Government, Hon. Sesan Olowa ; Ologunfayo of Ogunfolu Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, His Royal Majesty, Oba. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, right, Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on 25th of July, 2026,at Badagry Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7358" align="alignleft" width="932"] L-R: Chairman, Badagry Local Government, Hon. Babatunde Hunpe, APC Deputy Governor Gubernatorial Candidate in Lagos state, Princess. Damilola Sonayan James and Special Adviser on Environment, Engr.Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, engaged in cleaning during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held in Badagry Local Government on Saturday the 25th of July, 2026.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7357" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Ologunfayo of Ogunfayo Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, HRM Oba.
